plain: Carelessness or oversight that is not on purpose.

webster.text: A not turning the mind to; inattention; negligence; heedlessness.

example.quote: The respect which is felt for every portion of the constituted authorities forbids some of the reflections which this singular paragraph might excite; and they are the more readily suppressed, as it may be presumed, with justice perhaps as well as candor, that inadvertence may have had its share in the error.
example.cite: James Madison, Report on the Virginia Resolutions (Report of 1800), Jan. 7, 1800
